summary.intent: Clean up spec drift by auditing the spec criteria and the #290 tag guard against current code (read-only), and carry out four cleanup items: remove the dead `pending_pr_label` input, delete stale local branches and worktrees, plus the other listed cleanups.
summary.outcome: Launched five background audit agents (four spec-drift checks, one #290 audit). Deleted 11 local branches whose PRs were merged at the same tip, and removed the dead `pending_pr_label` input with a changeset in a signed commit on a cleanup branch. Contract tests passed. Audit results for spec drift were not yet reported and the release-PR-CI item was not addressed.

repo: Specs hold 251 criteria across five files: release (71), versioning (62), cli (55), workspace (39), matrix (24).

E180: GitHub refuses the workflow token pushing a tag at a commit not at a branch tip if its workflow files differ from every branch tip. A normal release is fine; recovering an older release (like 0.15.0 after main changed workflows) needs a person to push the tags with their own credential.
The recommended E180 handling is to document the manual tag push in `docs/releasing.md`, not to add a PAT or deploy key, which would conflict with the 'only the registry token' policy.
Removing a public action input requires a changeset (`.changeset/quick-hawks-swim.md`).
Action contract tests are run through `just` (workflow contracts recipe); the command guard accepts that but not direct invocation.

The #290 audit reported both tag guard gaps fixed: the log is uncapped (no `-n`) and two tests exist. Gap #2 (changes outside the package directory like `Cargo.lock`) was unverified by the agent, so the code was read directly.
The release PR gets no CI because the workflow token pushes the branch; a CI dispatch on that branch after refresh would fix it.
Worktree `ci/merge-group-trigger` belongs to another job and should be left alone.

code.finding: Defined the dead `pending_pr_label` input, now removed along with its uses in the release PR script and contract test.
Contained the pending label logic that was removed; the script structure was checked afterward.

workflow: Verify subagent audit claims by spot-checking key assertions directly before relying on them.
Classify local branches by PR state and tip match before deleting; only delete where a merged PR head equals the local tip so nothing unique is lost.
Use a scoped read-only audit with parallel background agents per spec file to cover many criteria cheaply.
The assistant guessed which item the user meant at one point and stated the guess explicitly so it could be corrected.

friction: Ambiguous user request ('cleanup spec drift') led the assistant to guess it meant E180 and explain that instead, until the user clarified with 'do the 4 cleanup'.
Running the action contract test directly was blocked by a guard; it had to be rerun via `just`.
A first attempt to run the contract test with output logged to a file preceded the working `just` approach.
One worktree branch could not be deleted because it belongs to another job.
open_items: Spec-drift audit results from the five background agents still need to be collected and acted on; the earlier review found about 14% of sampled criteria false or partly true.
